title: Adaptive kernel-aware probe and backstop routing for speculative streaming decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Draft design and implementation plan for a runtime component that: (1) issues small speculative prefill probes to fast model variants, (2) scores acceptance with a kernel-aware confidence metric, and (3) falls back to a robust backstop path when acceptance thresholds or kernel-affinity mismatches occur. The goal is to reduce end-to-end latency on common short-turn queries while keeping regression risk and cost bounded.
technical_summary: We will implement a narrow runtime layer (probe-orchestrator) that coordinates a two-phase decode: a lightweight speculative probe on a low-latency model (or optimized kernel path) followed by an authoritative decode on the primary model only if probe acceptance is low. The orchestrator is kernel-aware: it uses kernel fingerprinting and attention-profile heuristics to predict acceptance variance, and it biases probes to kernels likely to produce compatible KV cache shapes. Acceptance scoring blends token-level cross-entropy delta, KL divergence against the authoritative model on sampled prefixes (from offline calibration), and a latency delta margin. Fallback/backstop path includes a quick handoff with KV-cache harmonization or a soft-restart with graceful token replay when necessary.
design_decisions: Use small fixed-size probes (<=8 tokens prefill) to limit wasted compute and make acceptance signal timely
Normalize acceptance by kernel-specific baseline to avoid biasing probes against high-variance kernels
Prefer kernel candidates that share KV cache layout with the authoritative model to reduce handoff complexity
Implement probabilistic sampling of requests for offline dual-decode to maintain calibration datasets
Expose runtime flags for per-customer policy: aggressive, conservative, and disabled
rollout_plan: Step 0: Feature-flag the probe-orchestrator at the runtime level; default disabled for all customers
Step 1: Internal dogfood on synthetic low-latency workloads (high qps short-turn dialogs) with probes enabled; collect calibration telemetry
Step 2: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for customers opted-in to experimental 'fast-path' policy; monitor safety metrics and cost
Step 3: Expand to 25% with automated rollback triggers on regression or fallback rate thresholds; continue calibration
Step 4: Stabilize defaults and document per-customer tuning knobs in console
test_plan: Unit tests for probe lifecycle, acceptance scoring, and backstop activation
Integration tests across kernel variants and model families ensuring KV cache compatibility or safe replay behavior
Load tests with mixed sequence lengths to measure batching impact and cost delta
A/B evaluation using held-out prompt set for quality regression (automated eval harness)
Chaos test: force kernel mismatch / delayed probe response to validate graceful fallback and no double-charge scenarios
risks: Increased tail-cost if probes are overused without sufficient acceptance signal
Quality regressions if acceptance metric mis-calibrates for low-resource kernels
Operational complexity from KV cache harmonization across heterogeneous kernels
Billing/visibility concerns if speculative work is charged to customers incorrectly
next_steps: Build prototype probe-orchestrator and unit tests (Marco)
Run offline calibration using 50k sampled short-turn prompts to compute per-kernel acceptance baselines (Data team)
Design console controls and runtime flags for customer policies (Product)
Coordinate with billing to expose speculative compute on cost breakdowns (Finance)
Prepare runbook entries for fallback incidents and rollback criteria (SRE)
